subject: AstraSys dedicated pool: proposed regional split and SKU options
messages:
From: Tim Holt <tim.holt@astrasys.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: AstraSys Procurement <procurement@astrasys.com>, Nina Park <nina@edgeops.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: initial sizing conversation — dedicated footprint ask

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the call this morning. To follow up: procurement wants a simple, auditable proposal that shows how Redwood would split a dedicated pool for AstraSys across US/EU/APAC for our estimated workloads. Key constraints:

- Peak concurrent tokens: ~1.2M tokens/min during forecasted busy windows (we expect ~3 spikes/day).
- Average sustained: ~200k tokens/min.
- Residency: EU data must remain in EU region for EU users.
- Contract: 12 month committed capacity with quarterly checkpoints.

Could you provide a recommended pool split (nodes/instance SKUs), expected latency SLOs per region, and a rough monthly cost estimate for committed vs burst lanes? Procurement would also like SOC2 evidence and an SOW stub.

Can you send something by end of week? Procurement is on a tight cadence for Q1 approval.

Cheers,
Tim
Tim Holt
Head of Cloud Ops, AstraSys
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Holt <tim.holt@astrasys.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: initial sizing conversation — dedicated footprint ask

Hi Tim — great talking earlier.

High level, we can propose a tri-region dedicated architecture with:

- US primary pool (60% steady capacity + burst lanes)
- EU sovereign pool (25%) with data residency and separate KMS integration
- APAC pilot pool (15%) to cover peak latency-sensitive requests — can be resized after Q1 checkpoints

To make a concrete proposal we'll need:
1) Token distribution by region (rough % across US/EU/APAC during peaks)
2) Peak concurrency in RPS or sessions if available (helps us size KV cache heat)
3) Typical sequence lengths and ratio of chat vs. batch generation

I'll put together a sizing matrix and cost delta (committed vs burst) — draft by Friday EOD. Rishi/Ben — looping you for kernel/sku guidance and ops lead time.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 10:08:00 -0800
Subject: RE: internal — AstraSys tri-region sizing (input needed)

Team — capturing notes from Tim's ask. Need quick sanity check and numbers we can surface in the client proposal:

Context:
- Forecast peak: 1.2M tokens/min global spikes, with US heavy (roughly 65% of peak), EU 25%, APAC 10% initially.
- Sustained average: 200k tokens/min.
- Q1 contract: 12mo committed baseline with burst lanes at 2x committed for surge windows.

Questions:
- Rishi: for the EU pool with residency/KMS, recommend which instance SKUs and quantization profile to hit median p95 latency <= 220ms for chat (seq ~512). Also ops lead time for provisioning a dedicated EU pool (estimate days/weeks).
- Ben: cost delta for committed vs burst lanes (monthly commit pricing + burst overage model). Also ops notes about cross-region fallback policies if EU pool is saturated.
- Laura: procurement/commercial — minimum tranche and billing cadence we should propose to align with AstraSys procurement constraints.

Proposed quick numbers (need validation):
- US committed: equivalent of 48 x A200-type instances (continuous batch optimized) + 24 burst slots
- EU committed: 18 x A200-type + 8 burst slots (KMS + region-restricted routing)
- APAC committed: 8 x A200-type + 6 burst slots (pilot burst-heavy)

If those look sane, I'll fold into the draft SOW and pricing sheet.

Thanks —
Grace
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: RE: internal — AstraSys tri-region sizing (input needed)

Quick take after running ballpark sims with the infra team:

- Rishi's latency target (p95 <= 220ms at seq 512) is attainable with A200-class family on our continuous-batching path using int8 quant profile; recommend enabling prefix cache for known heavy flows.
- Cost estimates (monthly committed + 30% reserve for unexpected traffic):
  - US: committed $285k/mo, burst lanes (on-demand) add ~$95k/mo if used at 2x committed for spikes
  - EU: committed $110k/mo, burst add ~$38k/mo
  - APAC: committed $48k/mo, burst add ~$25k/mo (APAC higher per-unit infra cost)
- Ops lead time: EU pool with KMS and compliance checks ~18 business days to provision and run SOC2 evidence packaging; US pool ~10 business days; APAC pilot ~21 business days (edge onboarding and partner infra).

I'll attach a one-pager cost table and a draft SOW for Grace to send to Tim. Laura — commercial terms we should align on: quarterly usage checkpoint, 30-day termination notification for pilot tranche, and standard SLA with credit ladder.

Attachments: Redwood-proposal-AS-2027-0045-v1.pdf (draft pricing/SOW)

-ben
Ben Carter
Head of Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Holt <tim.holt@astrasys.com>, AstraSys Procurement <procurement@astrasys.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Nina Park <nina@edgeops.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 15:37:00 -0800
Subject: Proposal: tri-region dedicated footprint & SOW — AstraSys (AS-2027-0045)

Hi Tim / Procurement team — please find a draft proposal attached (Redwood-proposal-AS-2027-0045-v1.pdf) and a copy of the SOC2 evidence pointer (AstraSys-SOC2-evidence.pdf). Highlights below:

- Proposed committed split (monthly baseline):
  - US: 48 committed nodes (A200-class), 24 burst slots — targets p95 latency <= 200ms for typical chat seq 256, ~220ms for seq 512
  - EU (data-residency): 18 committed nodes, 8 burst slots — KMS integration and region routing enforced
  - APAC (pilot): 8 committed nodes, 6 burst slots — pilot clause at Q1 checkpoint to resize

- Pricing: committed monthly $443k (total across regions) with burst lanes billed at on-demand uplift; detailed cost table in attachment.
- Ops & provisioning: estimated stand-up timelines — US 10 business days, EU 18 business days (compliance, KMS), APAC 21 business days (partner edge onboarding).
- Contract terms suggested: 12-month commit, quarterly usage checkpoints with ability to resize committed baseline at checkpoint, 30-day notice for tranche reductions.

Next steps:
1) Procurement review — confirm SOW items and KMS requirements (do you need HSM integration?).
2) Sign-off on baseline and PO issuance to begin provisioning.
3) Provide a short telemetry sample (1-week token distribution by region) to finalize the cache sizing.

I've attached the docs and left placeholders for KMS endpoint and onboarding contacts. Happy to jump on a follow-up call early next week.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood-proposal-AS-2027-0045-v1.pdf; AstraSys-SOC2-evidence.pdf
From: Tim Holt <tim.holt@astrasys.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: AstraSys Procurement <procurement@astrasys.com>, Nina Park <nina@edgeops.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 Jan 2027 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: tri-region dedicated footprint & SOW — AstraSys (AS-2027-0045)

Grace — thanks, this is exactly the level of detail procurement wanted. A couple quick clarifications from procurement:

- EU KMS: we do require HSM-backed keys for EU workloads. Can Redwood support customer-managed HSM or a BYOK flow?
- Billing cadence: procurement prefers monthly invoice with quarterly reconciliation; is that compatible with your commercial team?
- Pilot clause: we'll accept the APAC pilot as written but request a concrete resizing SLA at the Q1 checkpoint.

I'll circulate the attached redlines from procurement (see attached) and aim to get a PO to you by end of next week, pending legal review.

Thanks again — looking forward to onboarding.

Tim
Head of Cloud Ops, AstraSys
Attachments: AstraSys-procurement-redlines.pdf
